title: Shift handover tactical bulletin — 2029-03-18
content:
Purpose:
This note captures the operational highlights for the outgoing shift, focused on three operational incidents, SLO health for the past 7 days, immediate runbook changes, and handoff pointers for the incoming on-call. Treat as the canonical short-form summary for the next 24–48h.

Attendees / Context:
- Author: Evelyn Chen (primary on-call)
- Collaborators who triaged: Marco Ruiz (serving-runtime), Samir Khan (autoscaler), Leah O'Connor (applied-ml ops)
- Outage window relevant to customer dashboards: 2029-03-16 -> 2029-03-17 UTC

Executive summary (1–2 lines):
- Two moderate incidents and one minor routing/quality incident this past 48h; combined caused a transient SLO breach for p95 latency and availability for hosted API. Short-term mitigations in place; follow-up action items assigned for durable fixes.

Incidents (chronological):
1) RUNTIME-KV-0316 (Major -> mitigated)
- Symptom: Sudden p99 inference latency spikes and increased 500/502 errors for embed/encode endpoints backed by opt-1.3b-quant.
- Timeline: First alerts 2029-03-16 02:13 UTC; full mitigation at 2029-03-16 05:02 UTC.
- Root cause (initial RCA): Aggressive KV-cache eviction triggered after a malformed long sequence stream from an internal eval job. The eviction caused heavy cache thrash and lock contention in the runtime’s KV store under our continuous-batching path.
- Immediate mitigation: Rolled back the eviction policy to previous threshold, paused the offending eval job, and rebalanced requests to healthy pods.
- Impact: ~18 minutes of elevated p99s before mitigation actions completed; customers saw ~2.1% increase in error rate during peak.
- Next steps: Patch in PR (linked) to add per-tenant eviction caps and a better backoff when eviction rate > X per minute. Owner: Marco. ETA: 2029-03-25.

2) AUTOSCALE-THRASH-0317 (Moderate -> mitigated)
- Symptom: Autoscaler repeatedly scaled up/down a dedicated pool (dedicated-east-1) causing transient capacity shortage and throttled queue leading to 429/503s for ~30m.
- Timeline: 2029-03-17 11:40–12:15 UTC.
- Root cause: Recent batching change reduced headroom on in-flight concurrency metric; autoscaler’s smoothing window was too short (30s), which made it responsive to very short bursts from a new customer workload (high token-rate but short requests). Result: unnecessary scale events.
- Mitigation: Increased autoscaler cooldown to 5m, increased smoothing window to 3m, and applied a temporary per-pool max-scale-rate limiter. Replayed the burst traffic in a canary to validate.
- Impact: Availability dip to 99.86% for that pool for the 30m window; overall hosted API availability affected but recovered after mitigation.
- Next steps: Revisit metric selection (use steady-state queue length instead of short-term in-flight) and add a synthetic test to catch thrash. Owner: Samir. ETA: 2029-03-22.

3) FALLBACK-ROUTE-QUALITY-0317 (Minor -> resolved)
- Symptom: Quality-monitoring evals surfaced an increase in semantic errors for several production routes that had automatically fallen back to a smaller model variant during the autoscale event.
- Timeline: flagged 2029-03-17 12:05 UTC; rollback at 12:20 UTC.
- Root cause: Fallback routing policy was overly permissive for routes with content-sensitivity tags; fallback-to-mini-model option was not gated by our quality-checks.
- Mitigation: Temporarily disabled automatic fallback for routes with tag:high-precision; rolled forward a stricter routing policy.
- Impact: Minor (customer-facing regression for a small subset of requests); no sustained outage.
- Next steps: Add a pre-fallback quality check in the routing layer. Owner: Leah. ETA: 2029-03-29.

SLO health (7-day window ending 2029-03-18):
- Latency SLOs (hosted text-generation, p95 < 450ms): p95 = 527ms (breach), p50 = 88ms, p99 = 1.2s.
- Availability SLO (>= 99.90% successful responses): 99.89% (marginal breach).
- Notes: The dominant contributors to SLO regression were KV-cache thrash (RUNTIME-KV-0316) and autoscaler thrash (AUTOSCALE-THRASH-0317). Token-cost per request rose ~4% during mitigation windows due to retries and fallbacks.

Runbook & procedural changes made during shift:
- KV-cache eviction runbook: added a new immediate action ("pause suspect evals") and a checklist to check eviction rate and tenant quotas. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/KV+Cache+Eviction+Policy
- Autoscaler runbook: added a new „cooldown validation“ step and a note to coordinate with applied-ml before deploying batching changes.
- Fallback routing: gated automatic fallback for routes with tag:high-precision; updated runbook to require a canary of 1% traffic before enabling fallback globally.

On-call handoff (incoming shift needs to know):
- Primary: @oncall-primary (Samir Khan) — contact via pager and #sre-ops Slack.
- Secondary: @oncall-secondary (Marco Ruiz).
- Active alerts to watch: SRE-KV-EVICT (threshold: eviction-rate > 10/min), SRE-AUTO-THRASH (scale-events/min > 2), SRE-FALLBACK-QUALITY (quality-drop > 5% vs baseline).
- Hot keys / dashboards: "KV cache telemetry", "Autoscaler events per pool", "Hosted API SLO overview" (org dashboard).

Action items (short list):
- Marco: Merge patch to add per-tenant eviction caps and add integration test for eviction backoff. ETA 2029-03-25.
- Samir: Update autoscaler metric to queue-length smoothing, add throttling test to CI to simulate short bursts. ETA 2029-03-22.
- Leah: Implement pre-fallback quality check in routing controller and add canary config. ETA 2029-03-29.
- Evelyn: Draft customer-facing incident summary for RUNTIME-KV-0316 (for CS review). ETA 2029-03-20.

Meeting notes & coordination items (today's sync):
- Rapid sync with applied-ml: need to gate large eval jobs that use long sequences or synthetic traffic; discuss quota enforcement.
- Platform / runtime: plan a small release to add eviction caps; will coordinate a 1-hour maintenance window next Tuesday to avoid customer impact.
- Observability: instrument eviction and eviction-backoff counters; add a dashboard panel to correlate eviction-rate with p99 latency.

Open questions and risks:
- Do we need per-tenant isolation for KV caches (memory-bound)? Short-term caps reduce blast radius, but long-term architecture change may be required. (Raised to design board)
- Autoscaler metric hygiene: which metric best predicts sustained capacity need without responding to short bursts?
- Fallback policy: what automated quality signal is cheap and robust enough to gate immediate fallback?

Notes to incoming on-call:
- If you see repeated small scale events within a 10–15m window, raise a bridge immediately (team: platform-eng + autoscale).
- Watch the evaluation job queue (internal-evals) and pause any job that looks like it pumps long sequences.
- If customer support escalates, reference incident RUNTIME-KV-0316 and set expectation that a patch is scheduled for 2029-03-25.

Appendix (quick links):
- KV eviction policy doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/KV+Cache+Eviction+Policy
- Jira tickets: SRE-4728 (KV eviction patch), SRE-4789 (autoscaler metric change)
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1823

End of bulletin.

Prepared by: Evelyn Chen (on-call)
Reviewed by: Marco Ruiz, Samir Khan
